If sentiment is consistently positive in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is negative in the last 3–5 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (8–14 days), adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is mixed or neutral in the last 5–7 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to mid-horizon (15–20 days) to hedge against volatility.

If sentiment is consistently negative in the last 5+ days, apply a 1–2% upward bias to late horizon (21–30 days) to counteract pessimism-driven price suppression.

If sentiment spikes positively after a prolonged negative trend, apply a 1–2% upward correction to late horizon (21–30 days) to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
